# An illustrative report, generated by the real report engine

[Open the sample PDF](sample-report.pdf) · [View the overview PNG](sample-report.png)

**DEMO / ILLUSTRATIVE DATA. Every number and publication in these files is
synthetic.** They show what Car Market's existing English report can explain;
they are not observed BMW prices, current inventory or national coverage.

The example selects BMW 218i Active Tourer in two scenario markets, NL and DE.
It contains 90 seeded publications per country: 86 across seven year,
transmission and mileage cohorts, three with a missing price/year/mileage,
and one with an unresolved model. The unchanged core selects 89 target catalog
IDs and 88 eligible prices per country. All IDs are provisional. There are no
VINs, registration plates, contacts, provider responses or physical-car joins.
The only example links use the reserved `.invalid` domain.

The first page shows the real core overview. The remaining eight pages show
its detailed charts, comparable groups and source volumes. Terracotta is NL;
green is DE. A large disclosure band is added to every page and the PNG.
Charts, numerical analysis, exclusions and the report's normal caveats come
from the existing generator, rather than hand-drawn estimates.

Read the supported group before the headline median. The best-supported
synthetic cohort is 2020 / automatic / 50–100k km, with 18 prices per scenario.
Its median is €23,200 for NL and €21,800 for DE. Another manual cohort has a
higher DE median. These invented differences demonstrate how the report
separates a matched group from the overall distribution. They are not import
savings: trim, generation, actual condition and import costs are not controlled.
Unknown fields stay unknown.

## Three different clocks

| Clock | Fixed illustrative value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic record clock | 15 January 2026, 10:00 UTC | Timestamp assigned to the seeded observations. No HTTP capture took place. |
| Analysis cut-off | 15 January 2026, 12:00 UTC | The explicit `as_of` of this scenario. |
| Example generation clock | 15 January 2026, 12:05 UTC | Reproducible report/snapshot/PDF metadata for the demonstration. |

These clocks are not today's market confirmations. The example uses the normal
13-hour analysis window relative to its fixed cut-off; eligibility in this
scenario says nothing about real market freshness. Actual execution times
are kept separately in the private build proof and do not renew any source data.

## Reproduce the assets

From a source development environment with the existing reports extra and
`pypdf` development dependency available:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python docs/media/render_sample_report.py
```

The helper seeds disposable databases, calls `car_market.analytics.generate`,
adds only the DEMO bands and combines the actual overview/details PDFs. It
replaces these two example assets. It does not accept an existing database,
provider URL or native fixture. Scratch databases and intermediate output are
removed on completion. No SQLite, raw data, exports or credentials belong in
this media directory.

The dataset, provisional-ID allocation and example clocks are fixed.
`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` fixes PDF timestamps. The core source input is
`cc7b69d51aae49de71462637c0157ab204088092`; the runtime files are unchanged.
The helper uses temporary in-process clock/UUID adapters only for synthetic
seeding and demo metadata, without editing the runtime. Byte reproducibility
applies to the checked dependency/font environment; this does not promise
identical bytes across every future rendering-library version.

Project code uses MIT. The report uses the bundled Lato fonts under their
existing SIL Open Font License. This sample is a design demonstration, not
a new provider, product/runtime change or release acceptance certificate.
